statement: A beam is one physical member from support to support, measured over its DRAWN plan (between its drawn edge lines, up to the faces of the members it frames into) at its full section. A member SUPPORTS the beam only when it starts below the beam and continues to its soffit (a column / neck under the slab, a bearing wall, a beam the beam frames into); a member that STARTS on the beam (planted column, the turned upper part of a turned column) is CARRIED. (1) The beam is cut only at a supporting member, and only over that member's footprint: the part of the cut beside a support narrower than the beam, inside the drawn beam edges, stays in the beam. (2) A cut at a carried member is refused: the beam is continuous under it and owns the whole region (a route G hold 'unlabelled span across a support' at a carried member is resolved: one member, one label). (3) A piece that stops at a carried member's face, or square to a member it meets obliquely, is short by the drawn beam beyond its face up to the supporting / receiving face. (4) Where a beam piece is billed THROUGH a supporting column's footprint while the column line in the same state also bills it (full storey interval, or a ledger joint line), the intersection is DOUBLE and the precedence column > beam decides (the beam line is over-billed by share x A x D); a column record built to the soffit of the member billed through it (R-PLANTED-COL-1) is not double. (5) A shortfall is claimed only where the beam's drawn edges run on over it (else the drawn beam ends at the billed face: PASS; drawn in part: HELD, bounded); a projection strip or a width conflict keeps its region HELD; nothing is ever closed by 0.
